report: Reassessed the complete claim: reject repeated named fields within a struct or single enum variant, while allowing reuse between declarations and variants. Verified validate.rs and value_types.rs exactly match the historical source snapshots; the historical rationale remains supported by current inputs. The single ordinary implementation association is in Model::check_values: check_fields creates a new BTreeSet on each call and reports failed field-name insertion; structs call it once and named variants each call it separately. Model::check invokes check_values and returns its diagnostics. The complete associated test set is the single ordinary field_names_are_unique_only_within_their_own_payload test. Its two rejection cases assert exactly one duplicate-field diagnostic for struct and named variant; its positive case asserts no diagnostics for reuse between two structs and two variants, also reusing the same name across these declaration kinds. Thus removing rejection or wrongly sharing the name set would be detected. Captured check/parse_body setup helpers show these assertions consume actual parse-and-validate results. No TODO/N/A evidence or outstanding prerequisites. This is source inspection and byte comparison; I ran review start/read/record, not behavior tests or a workspace build. Coordinator-reported passing tests/build are separate execution evidence. No edits required.
